content:
A cautious line-by-line translation, preserving damaged/uncertain places:

1. When, in far-off days, the days—heaven and earth in their proper places—had been fashioned,  
2. when, in far-off nights, the nights—heaven and earth in their proper places—had been fashioned,  
3. when, in far-off years, the years and their destinies had been decreed,  
4. when the Anunna gods had been born,  
5. when the mother-goddesses / divine mothers had been allotted high status,  
6. when the mother-goddesses had been apportioned between heaven and earth,  
7. when the mother-goddesses had […] conceived and given birth,  
8. when the gods’ food-rations […] had been assigned/bound to their dining-halls/shrines,  
9. the great gods were in charge of the work, while the lesser gods carried the toil.  
10. The gods dug canals; they heaped up their silt in Ḫarali.  
11. The gods worked/kneaded the clay; they began to complain about their lives.  

12. At that time, he of broad wisdom, the begetter/fashioner among all the great gods—  
13. Enki—in the Engur, the deep wellspring of flowing water, a place whose interior no god could fathom,  
14. lay in his bed and did not rise from sleep.  
15. The gods were shedding tears; they were making lamentation.  
16. But the one lying in sleep did not rise from his bed.  

17. Namma, the primeval mother, who had given birth to all the great gods,  
18. brought the tears of the gods before her son.  
19. “Are you really lying there? Are you really sleeping?  
20. […] you do not get up!  
21. The gods whom your hands fashioned […] are bearing/complaining under their burden.”  

Several lines, especially 7–8 and 19–21, are fragmentary or lexically uncertain, so the translation there is approximate.
